review_notes: I read both proofs in full. The normalization block (hm, hr2, hr, c, z and the four bullets) is the same in both, line for line. The differences are the test family (Unit vs Option I) and the arithmetic that produces hb. In the first theorem hb comes from `nlinarith [mul_pos hδ (sub_pos.mpr hr2)]`, and in the other from `nlinarith` with δ ≤ ε/4. NormalizedExpectationRoots.lean is already imported by the target, so a shared lemma there creates no cycle. I did not check that `finiteVectorDensityTensor_norm_sq` and `densityRoot_norm` are visible in NormalizedExpectationRoots.lean. I assumed they are, because `expectation_unit_intertwiners` already uses them there. The local `NormedSpace`/`NormSMulClass` instances in that file would apply to the new lemma statement, but I did not check how the target file gets the same instances. `expectation_unit_intertwiners` appears to have no uses in the repo beyond its declaration (grep found only the declaration). This does not change the verdict, since the duplication is still real. I found no other repeated machinery in lines 1–233. The later theorems are short, with distinct bookkeeping. Examples are the epsilon splitting in `expectation_spatial_finite_approximation`, the min/square step in `expectation_spatial_norm_approximation`, and the real/imaginary split in `expectation_complex_spatial_approximation`.

claims.reason: The two proofs repeat the same nontrivial argument. It normalizes a near-unit finite density root r into the unit vector (‖r‖⁻¹)•r and carries four properties across: norm 1, positivity, the finite-rank submodule, and the squared unitary-defect bound via ‖r‖²>1/2. The hm derivation from the trace-of-1 test is also copied. Both blocks use the same hypotheses: τ normalized, δ ≤ 1/2, and the same hru/hrp/hrs data. The two proofs differ only in the test family and in the constant arithmetic (2δ vs ε). A lemma in NormalizedExpectationRoots.lean, which the target already imports, avoids any cycle. The lemma needs only δ ≤ 1/2, |1-‖r‖²|<δ, positivity of hsOperator r, and a finite-range F. δ>0 follows from the absolute-value hypothesis. For the existing theorem, δ=min(ε/4,1/2) gives 2δ ≤ ε/2 < ε. The refactor would remove about 45 duplicated lines and keep one copy of the normalization argument.
claims.shared_lemma: lemma unit_normalization {δ : ℝ} (r : NuclearUltrapower.HilbertSchmidt H) (hδ : δ ≤ 1/2) (hm : |1 - ‖r‖^2| < δ) (hrp : 0 ≤ NuclearUltrapower.hsOperator r) (hrs : ∃ F : Submodule ℂ H, FiniteDimensional ℂ F ∧ ∀ y, NuclearUltrapower.hsOperator r y ∈ F) : 1/2 < ‖r‖^2 ∧ ‖(((‖r‖⁻¹ : ℝ) : ℂ)) • r‖ = 1 ∧ 0 ≤ NuclearUltrapower.hsOperator ((((‖r‖⁻¹ : ℝ) : ℂ)) • r) ∧ (∃ F : Submodule ℂ H, FiniteDimensional ℂ F ∧ ∀ y, NuclearUltrapower.hsOperator ((((‖r‖⁻¹ : ℝ) : ℂ)) • r) y ∈ F) ∧ ∀ (U : _), ‖NuclearUltrapower.hsConjugation U r - r‖^2 < δ → ‖NuclearUltrapower.hsConjugation U ((((‖r‖⁻¹ : ℝ) : ℂ)) • r) - (((‖r‖⁻¹ : ℝ) : ℂ)) • r‖^2 < 2*δ. Also lemma norm_sq_eq_of_trace_one_test (τ) (w) (hw) (x) {δ} (h : |(τ.functional 1).re - ∑ k, w k * (inner ℂ (x k) (x k)).re| < δ) : |1 - ‖NuclearUltrapower.densityRoot (finiteVectorDensityTensor w x)‖^2| < δ. Proof sketch: it is the existing block. abs_lt and linarith give 1/2<‖r‖², then 0<‖r‖. The remaining parts use norm_smul with inv_mul_cancel₀, map_smul with smul_nonneg, F.smul_mem, and map_smul/←smul_sub/norm_smul with inv_mul_lt_iff₀ and nlinarith [mul_pos hδ0 (sub_pos.mpr hr2)].

Use `hm := norm_sq_eq_of_trace_one_test τ w hw x (ha ())`, `obtain ⟨_, hzn, hzp, hzF, hzU⟩ := unit_normalization r (min_le_right _ _) hm hrp hrs`, and close the defect with `fun j => by rw [hsLeft_sub_right_norm]; have := hzU _ (hru j); linarith [min_le_left (ε/4) (1/2)]`. The theorem shrinks to about 15 lines.
